size.note: Wikipedia gives 15–16 cm and a weight of 41 g. Females average slightly larger than males.

habitat: Wetlands, walking on lily pads and aquatic grasses.
summary: The smallest jacana. White breast, golden forehead, cinnamon crown and a dark eyestripe. The mantle and wings are darker, and the wings have a white trailing edge in flight. The sexes are nearly identical. Males have darker backs. Wikipedia does not say whether it is resident. The most common call is a low woot from both sexes. The distress chatter is hwi hwi hwi. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

similar.note: An immature African Jacana has a black crown and an eyestripe and can look like an adult Lesser Jacana. Lesser Jacana is the small bird, with a cinnamon crown and a white breast. In flight it shows a white trailing edge.

sources.title: The Atlas of Southern African Birds, Vol. 1 (Lesser Jacana)

calls.description: The most common call is a melodic, low woot from both sexes. A distress chatter is hwi hwi hwi. No grade A or B recording was in the set. Grade C call from Kasanka, Zambia, when the bird was flushed. The filename names Lesser Jacana. It was not cleaned.

research.note: No Newman page was found. Wikipedia does not state residency, so status and months were left unset. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged. Population figures were left unchanged. Status is still omitted: SABAP1 finds no seasonality but says it moves in response to its ephemeral habitat.
